title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving assistance for wash to the most vulnerable communities in rural areas in Baidoa

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtBaidoa District remains one of the most critical humanitarian hotspots in southern Somalia, driven by prolonged drought, recurrent climatic shocks, and sustained displacement pressures. The Bay Region hosts hundreds of thousands of internally displaced persons (IDPs), with Baidoa serving as a primary hub for communities fleeing drought, food insecurity, and livelihood collapse in surrounding rural areas.ltbrgtRecent IPC analyses (2025) classify parts of Bay in Crisis (IPC Phase 3) and Emergency (IPC Phase 4), underscoring the convergence of water scarcity, food insecurity, and heightened health risks. According to UN OCHA, 6.9 million people across Somalia require humanitarian assistance in 2025, including over 4.3 million children. The Bay Region consistently ranks among the areas with the highest severity and persistent unmet needs.ltbrgtRural Baidoa continues to experience acute service deficits, as consecutive below-average rainfall seasons in 2024–2025 have severely undermined water availability and basic WASH infrastructure. Assessments indicate that over 60% of water sources in drought-affected areas are either non-functional or operating below sustainable yield, forcing households to travel long distances or rely on unsafe surface water sources. These gaps in WASH services translate directly into life-threatening public health risks. National WASH data show that 6.6 million people in Somalia lack access to safe water, and only 52% of the population has access to basic water services.ltbrgtIn Baidoa’s rural settlements, households increasingly depend on costly emergency water supply systems, with prices often exceeding USD 6–8 per 200-liter barrel during peak dry Jilaal periods (January–March), significantly limiting water consumption and hygiene practices. Limited household water treatment and poor source protection increase contamination risks. Disease surveillance confirms that drought-affected districts with disrupted WASH services remain highly vulnerable to outbreaks. AWD/cholera monitoring over recent years shows that areas experiencing water scarcity and sanitation breakdown consistently account for a high proportion of suspected cases nationally.ltbrgtTo address these urgent needs, WARDO proposes to deliver life-saving emergency WASH assistance to drought-affected rural communities in Baidoa District through an integrated WASH package comprising:-ltbrgt* Sustained and Emergency Water Supply: (1) 60 days of emergency water supply for 1,666 households (10,000 people) and (2) rehabilitation of three strategic water sources (one borehole and two shallow wells) equipped with solar-powered pumping systems, serving approximately 8,000 people. (3) Conducting routine water quality monitoring, chlorination, and establishment/training of three Water Management Committees.ltbrgt* Soft WASH Activities : (4) Distribution of 20 sanitation toolkits and (5) implementation of 20 community clean-up campaigns and maintaining hygiene standards through (6) distribution of 1,780 hygiene kits targeting 12,000 people and (7) delivery of 32 targeted hygiene promotion and education sessions at community and facility levels.ltbrgtThe project will prioritize vulnerable rural communities, with a particular focus on women, girls, and persons with disabilities, providing immediate life-saving support to approximately 12,000 individuals (3,661 women, 3,864 girls, 2,441 men, and 2,034 boys).This intervention aims to mitigate the impacts of drought and displacement, reduce waterborne disease transmission, and strengthen community resilience to ongoing climatic shocks.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
